what.text: People have experienced internal displacement inside Somalia, while refugees from Somalia reside in host countries including Kenya, Ethiopia, Uganda, Germany, and Yemen.
At the end of 2025, 3347408 people were living in internal displacement inside Somalia because of conflict and violence.
At the end of 2025, there were 319471 refugees from Somalia living in Kenya.

why.text: Armed conflict over the government of Somalia was active from 2006 to 2025 between the Government of Somalia and opposition groups ARS/UIC, Al-Shabaab, and Hizbul Islam.

Armed conflict over Somaliland territory, Somalia occurred in 2018 involving the Republic of Somaliland, while Armed conflict with the Islamic State group, Somalia was active from 2019 to 2021 and in 2025 involving IS.
In addition to armed conflicts, disaster hazards recorded in Somalia include Drought and Flood.

when.text: The number of people living in internal displacement inside Somalia because of conflict and violence stood at 824551 at the end of 2017.
In 2023, new internal displacements inside Somalia from disasters reached 2043426 movements during the year.
During these same years, armed conflict over the government of Somalia remained active.

how.text: The sources don't say which specific routes displaced people take or what their living conditions are.
Conflict internal displacement is measured as year-end totals of people protected or assisted by UNHCR, alongside year-end population estimates by IDMC.
Disaster displacement statistics record the count of new movements during each year rather than individual people.
